item.content:encoded:
I could understand the horror of being suddenly and irrevocably aged by itself. One of my phobias is to be in a body that is not my own. Then the secondary effects came up.
Sudden advancement without any medicine or treatment beyond what the body should have allowed really upped the body horror.
The changing face and rotation at first sound benign, but someone who happens upon it would be fascinated and may stay near or tell their friends…
Very nice.

item.title: Re: Rewrite of Article
item.content:encoded:
If you're doing something that is obvious (such as a clock that messes with the aging rate of everything around it), your best bet is probably to amp up the emotional impact. "Spelling it out" is optional, if you can find a way to make the reader feel something, like anger at lazy maintenance men that got half a dozen people killed, without having to infodump on the effect.

TL,DR version: If you're not gonna throw a curveball, throw a fastball.

item.title: Rewrite of Article
item.content:encoded:
I've taken some of the advice from the review and tried to expand the article. Rather than simply fold descriptions into the original article or try to change the original author's wording much more than I already have (I adopted this one a couple of years ago), I added on the letter at the end to try and make the impact of the SCP a little stronger felt. Since the doctor in question is planning it as a giant guilt trip, I think it manages to avoid being too narmy. Let me know if I'm wrong.

Also, I took Rioghail's advice to heart and moved the containment procedures around a bit to get things better in place. Can't do too much about the writing style, but I hope it… err… Irks you less.

In short, even if I didn't take your advice, thanks Roget, Moose, Scantron, Harland, Vince, Rioghail, and ksaid for your feedback. Hope everyone likes the changes.

item.title: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
I'm calling for a review of this article. Please read it, vote, and comment if you haven't already done so.

While the idea behind it is workable, other articles have done similar concepts with better execution. This one just feels incredibly blunt, with no subtlety to its execution. I just feel like it would be so much more interesting if it would just tell us the details of the effect, rather than skimping or expunging anything that might pique the interest of the reader. An expanded version of this could be stellar.
